# SE-EDU Git conventions

Use the SE-EDU Git conventions at https://se-education.org/guides/conventions/git.html for all future commits in this repository.

Mandatory requirements for every commit:

- Write a clear commit subject line in the imperative mood.
- Capitalize the first letter of the subject line.
- Do not end the subject line with a period.
- Keep the subject line to 50 characters if possible and never exceed 72 characters.
- Optional scope or category prefixes are allowed when helpful.
- For non-trivial changes, add a body after a blank line.
- Wrap the body at 72 characters.
- Explain WHAT the change is and WHY it was done, not HOW it was implemented.
- Use bullet points where they improve readability.
- Keep each commit focused on one concern or one change set.
- When proposing or creating a commit message, include enough detail to explain the rationale.

This project also follows the repository-specific Git rule:

- Use lightweight tags unless the user explicitly requests an annotated tag.
